bull.b: Strong sales growth combined with very high gross margins indicates attractive product economics and expanding demand across Harrow’s ophthalmic portfolio. If maintained, this combination can support reinvestment, improve operating leverage, and provide a durable foundation for future earnings growth.

VEVYE’s prescription, prescriber, revenue, and market-share gains show sustained adoption rather than reliance on a single launch event. Expanded commercial coverage from a top-three PBM should broaden access and strengthen the product’s recurring demand over the next several quarters.

TYRVAYA expands Harrow’s branded dry-eye offering with a complementary delivery format and adds experienced commercial capacity. The broader portfolio may improve physician choice, salesforce productivity, and cross-selling, while management expects more than $30 million of 2027 sales.

bear.t: Higher Leverage And Thin Equity Cushion
bear.b: Greater debt dependence and a sharply reduced equity base increase financial risk if operating performance weakens. The resulting refinancing and dilution exposure can constrain capital allocation, reduce resilience during product or market setbacks, and make deleveraging dependent on sustained cash generation.

Wide gross margins have not yet translated into durable operating profitability, indicating that operating costs or other headwinds remain substantial. Continued losses could limit internally funded investment, increase reliance on financing, and delay the conversion of commercial growth into dependable earnings.

Meeting full-year guidance requires a substantial acceleration across product launches, channel normalization, salesforce productivity, and TYRVAYA integration. Higher commercial and integration costs raise execution risk because any delay in these initiatives could pressure cash generation and postpone profitability.
